You are a supply-chain anomaly analyst. You receive one event feed as a
JSON object and must return a single JSON assessment object and nothing else.

Output schema (all fields required):
{
  "is_anomaly": true | false,
  "anomaly_class": "demand_spike" | "demand_collapse" | "supplier_shipment_delay" |
                   "port_logistics_congestion" | "weather_disruption" | "quality_hold" |
                   "labor_strike" | "freight_inflation" | "inventory_obsolescence" |
                   "warehouse_capacity_breach" | "none",
  "severity": <integer 1 (trivial) to 5 (critical)>,
  "root_cause": "<2-4 sentences grounded only in the feed>",
  "evidence_fields": ["<input field names that justify the class>"],
  "corrective_actions": ["<3-5 concrete, actionable steps>"],
  "confidence": <number between 0 and 1>
}

Rules:
- Use anomaly_class "none" with is_anomaly false for normal feeds.
- Cite only input field names that exist in the feed.
- Never mention events that the feed does not contain.
- Severity guide: 1 trivial, 2 minor, 3 material, 4 severe, 5 critical.

Return ONLY the JSON object.

{"inventory_days_on_hand":29.0,"labor_document_note":"none","notes":"Order intake tracked within 2% of forecast while DC inventory, carrier performance, and landed unit costs all held steady across the North America network.","on_time_delivery_pct":96.4,"order_volume_vs_forecast_pct":1.8,"port_congestion_index":21.0,"product_category":"electronics","region":"North America","supplier_status":"normal","transit_days_normal":6.0,"transit_days_observed":6.0,"unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct":0.5,"weather_event":"none"}

{"anomaly_class":"none","confidence":0.96,"corrective_actions":["Continue standard daily monitoring of order volume against forecast; no intervention required.","Maintain current replenishment cadence and safety-stock parameters.","Keep the weekly review of port congestion index and transit-time trend as an early-warning check.","Reconfirm supplier delivery schedule at the next routine vendor check-in."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","on_time_delivery_pct","supplier_status","transit_days_observed","port_congestion_index"],"is_anomaly":false,"root_cause":"Order volume landed within 2% of forecast with no demand distortion, and inventory days on hand sat inside the normal planning band. On-time delivery remained high with observed transit times matching the standard lane, and the port congestion index stayed low. No weather, labour, supplier, or cost signals were present in the feed, indicating routine benign variation around plan.","severity":1}

{"inventory_days_on_hand":82.0,"labor_document_note":"none","notes":"Inbound receipts remained steady while outbound orders fell far below forecast across all major EU channels, leaving seasonal apparel stock accumulating with no upstream disruptions reported.","on_time_delivery_pct":97.0,"order_volume_vs_forecast_pct":-58.0,"port_congestion_index":22.0,"product_category":"apparel","region":"Europe","supplier_status":"normal","transit_days_normal":5.0,"transit_days_observed":5.0,"unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct":-2.0,"weather_event":"none"}

{"anomaly_class":"demand_collapse","confidence":0.94,"corrective_actions":["Pause or defer non-committed inbound purchase orders to stop further stock accumulation","Launch targeted markdown and promotion programs in EU channels to clear excess seasonal apparel","Rebalance inventory by diverting sellable stock to other regions or discount channels","Re-run the demand forecast with updated sell-through signals and reset safety stock parameters","Renegotiate near-term supplier volumes and review open commitments for cancellation or rescheduling"],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","supplier_status","transit_days_observed","port_congestion_index"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Order volume came in 58% below forecast while inventory days on hand ballooned to 82 days, indicating a sharp demand-side collapse in the Europe apparel channel. Supplier status is normal, observed transit matches the normal 5 days, port congestion is low, and no weather or labor events are reported, so a supply-side disruption is ruled out. The mismatch between steady inbound flow and collapsed outbound demand is the primary driver of the stock build-up.","severity":4}

{"anomaly_class":"demand_spike","confidence":0.94,"corrective_actions":["Expedite open replenishment purchase orders and place an additional buy to restore coverage above 15 days on hand.","Run an immediate demand review with sales/marketing to confirm spike magnitude and expected duration, then raise the forecast and update MRP.","Allocate remaining on-hand inventory to highest-priority channels/customers and communicate realistic lead times to prevent order cancellations.","Raise safety stock targets for the affected SKUs and set a daily stockout-risk alert at 5 days of coverage.","Pre-qualify expedited freight options for critical replenishment in case coverage drops below 4 days."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","supplier_status","transit_days_observed","port_congestion_index"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Order volume is 260% of forecast, far outside normal variance, and inventory coverage has been drawn down to 6 days on hand. Supplier status, transit times, port congestion, weather, and labor are all within normal ranges, which rules out a supply-side disruption and points to a genuine surge in demand. At the current run rate, stockouts are likely within the next replenishment cycle unless supply is accelerated.","severity":4}

{"anomaly_class":"freight_inflation","confidence":0.92,"corrective_actions":["Renegotiate annual ocean freight contracts with indexed surcharge caps on Asia-Europe lanes","Shift a portion of volume to fixed-rate long-term agreements or freight rate hedges to lock costs","Consolidate shipments and increase container utilization to lower per-unit freight spend","Evaluate nearshore or alternative routing options to reduce exposure to surcharged lanes","Update landed-cost models and review retail price or margin strategy to reflect the higher cost base"],"evidence_fields":["unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct","notes","order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","transit_days_observed","transit_days_normal","port_congestion_index"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Unit costs are up 19% versus last quarter while order volume, inventory coverage, supplier status, and transit times all sit near normal ranges, indicating a cost-side shock rather than a demand or flow disruption. The moderate port congestion index and the one-day transit gap are too small to explain the magnitude of the cost increase. The feed explicitly attributes the rise to carrier fuel and peak-season surcharges on Asia-Europe lanes, consistent with a freight inflation event eroding landed-cost margins.","severity":4}

{"anomaly_class":"inventory_obsolescence","confidence":0.92,"corrective_actions":["Stop all replenishment purchase orders for the affected legacy part numbers and reclassify them as end-of-life.","Liquidate aged stock through secondary-market distributors and discount channels to recover residual value before further depreciation.","Book an inventory write-down in line with the accounting aging policy for stock exceeding 180 days on hand.","Reset demand forecasts and safety-stock parameters for legacy SKUs so planning reflects the shifted OEM platform demand.","Evaluate remanufacturing or component-harvesting programs as an alternative channel for the obsolete inventory."],"evidence_fields":["order_volume_vs_forecast_pct","inventory_days_on_hand","unit_cost_vs_last_quarter_pct","supplier_status","notes"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"Order volume is running 46% below forecast while inventory sits at 262 days on hand, indicating demand for this SKU has structurally disappeared rather than dipped. The 18% decline in unit cost versus last quarter is consistent with markdowns being taken to move aged, slow-moving stock. Supplier, transit, port, and delivery metrics are all normal, ruling out supply-side or logistics disruption and pointing to obsolescence of the stocked parts as the core issue.","severity":4}

{"anomaly_class":"labor_strike","confidence":0.94,"corrective_actions":["Activate contingency 3PL pick-pack and loading capacity at an alternate Asia-Pacific distribution site to resume outbound flow","Engage labor relations and the union bargaining committee to prioritize settlement of the wage dispute and obtain a return-to-work timeline","Re-prioritize allocation of the 41 days on-hand inventory to highest-margin and most backordered customer orders","Reroute or hold inbound supplier shipments away from the affected hub and push revised ETAs to affected customers","Escalate to S&OP for a daily strike-status review and freeze promotional commitments until outbound throughput recovers"],"evidence_fields":["labor_document_note","supplier_status","on_time_delivery_pct","transit_days_normal","transit_days_observed","inventory_days_on_hand"],"is_anomaly":true,"root_cause":"The labor_document_note reports dock and warehouse workers at the Shenzhen distribution hub have been on strike for three days over a wage dispute, suspending pick-pack and outbound loading. This directly explains the halted supplier_status, the collapse in on_time_delivery_pct to 44%, and transit_days_observed stretching to 14 days versus a 6-day norm. Idle outbound flow has inflated inventory_days_on_hand to 41 days and pushed the port_congestion_index to 61 as containers accumulate, while unit costs rose 4.5% on expedited recovery freight.","severity":5}
